Root cause to fix once: the structural lane evaluates utility types over a LOSSY collected model (index signatures, readonly, declaration scope, builtin identity, undefined/never are not recorded) and so asserts exactness it cannot prove. Introduce the invariant 'structural expansion is exact or declined': an expansion proceeds only when every input fact it relies on is recorded and complete (declared fidelity: no index signature, modifiers known or irrelevant, binding resolved in the right scope to the builtin, no optional-undefined edge); otherwise the application stays as the named type (the checker lane, ADR 0026's type authority, answers it). 0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md
9:tsrs (`oxc-project/tsrs`, Apache-2.0) is a Rust port of the TypeScript 7 checker at microsoft/TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`, the commit `typescript@7.1.0-beta` was built from. It speaks the same `--api` protocol: the 19 methods caliper calls are all present, and 87 one-prop fixtures got the same oracle verdicts as `typescript-beta`. A throwaway prototype through the Node client (not in the repository; these numbers are the record) measured on Chakra `ButtonProps` (1,138 props) a 43-47 ms snapshot and the first converted prop at 62-67 ms, where ADR 0022 measured 703 ms with `tsc` on a different program root (indicative, not an A/B), with tsrs peaking at 126-130 MiB. On 16 hand-written components the checker was equal or better on 14, worse on union member order and an unresolvable import. A polymorphic component instantiated through a virtual file gave 267 props for `'div'` where both engines give 2 today. tsrs's own benchmark (`bench/RESULTS.md`) reports 1.8 to 4.2 times TypeScript 7.1 beta's speed and 2.1 to 2.6 times less memory.
20:- **Pin.** We pin exact tsrs crates (`tsrs_api` and `tsrs_vfs` `=0.24.0`, TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`) and bump them on purpose, never through dependabot (its ignore list); the npm `tsrs` the parity gate runs (`apps/oracle`, `0.24.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the same TypeScript commit) moves with them, and `scripts/check-packaging.mjs` fails while the two name different releases. A bump passes the deterministic construct suite (`apps/oracle/construct-suite`, being built on `feat/construct-suite`) and a tsrs-against-Go parity run of it. The weekly oracle keeps the Go `typescript` checker: an oracle running the checker that produced the answer agrees with it by construction.
21:- **Linked.** The product links the tsrs crates and asks `tsrs_api::Session` in process, on one thread with a 512 MiB stack, the stack the `tsrs` binary serves on; nothing is installed, and there is no other checker to choose. The Go `typescript` beta is the oracle, the construct goldens and the parity gate, in `apps/oracle` only. The linked checker is never replaced, since a fresh session raises this process's memory rather than returning it; past `OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, read from its own arenas, it stops for the session and components keep their structural answer with a diagnostic. A panic closes its session and a fresh one answers the next request, and a file nested past 20,000 brackets is not given to it (trail 369 slice 2).
37:Migration, each slice behind a deterministic gate, none on the oracle. The tsrs backend (the Rust client running on tsrs, PR 390) is done.
52:- The checker lane of the construct suite (caliper's checker path over `apps/oracle/construct-suite`) shows no regression against the structural path except listed improvements. **PASS**: `just test-checker-lane` on the S8 branch.
56:- The tsrs-against-Go parity check (`pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity`, PR 392) passes on the pinned version, and runs on every pin change. **PASS**: 235 of 235 rows identical on `tsrs` `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, none allow-listed; again on `0.24.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the release the product links, in trail 369 slice 4.

index signature or an unfound parent as all its keys.
